generations.prompt: An old woman in a mustard cardigan sits on a timber porch in warm late-afternoon sun beside a small cloth-covered device on a table. She lifts her eyes from the device to the sunlit field in front of her, and with a small gesture of one hand toward the light she says, simply, a statement about the evening. She speaks a soft, unfamiliar, vowel-rich language of her own, not English, with the stress late in each word. She says: "Noréla tové seli ené." (no-réh-la toh-véh seh-lee eh-néh). Then she looks back down at the device and waits, lips closed. Sound: her voice, wind in dry grass, insects. The camera is locked off and does not move. No music. No subtitles, captions or on-screen text of any kind.
